description: Surface Water Integrated Modeling, or SWIM, is a Julia package developed by SINTEF Digital for analysing surface-water accumulation from terrain. Its spill-point algorithms identify catchments, waterways and connected ponds, with extensions for precipitation, simplified infiltration and overflow through time. Buildings, obstacles and drainage measures can be represented in the terrain workflow. These outputs support rapid urban-flood screening and comparisons of local adaptation measures. The software is geographically portable; extent and resolution follow the terrain data. A documented example uses a district in central Oslo. The code and examples are free on GitHub under Apache-2.0 and the package is available through the Julia registry. A limitation is its simplified spill-point and infiltration representation; it does not establish the accuracy of a full hydrodynamic flood model. No directly related catalogue record was established. This review inspected metadata and documentation without running the Oslo example or obtaining elevation data.
inputs: Terrain topography and infrastructure or obstacle representation
name: SWIM Surface Water Integrated Modeling
notes: G5 G5-0088. Software checked through metadata and documentation, without installation or execution. Geographic scope follows the documented application or software portability; it does not imply validation throughout that area.
